I am 48 years old, a farmer in Quzhou County, Hebei. I finished middle school. I have only been farming my own 10.1 mu for 2 years, so I still watch what my neighbors do and copy the ones who get good results. Old Wang next door has grown eggplant for over 10 years, and he told me eggplant is a "heavy eater" — if you starve it, you get nothing. I learned that the hard way last year when I tried to save 20 yuan per mu on fertilizer and my eggplant turned yellow.

My farm is 10.1 mu. I plant 4 mu of eggplant, 2 mu of chili, and the remaining 4.1 mu I do wheat in winter and maize in summer. That fills the land completely.

For eggplant this year, I will use hybrid seed. I will put 26 kg of nitrogen per mu, 10 kg phosphorus, and 16 kg potassium. I figure this from 50 jin of urea plus compound fertilizer and potash. I will irrigate 7 times from May to August and spray pesticide 5 times because the fruit borer was bad last year. I expect 3800 kg per mu if the frost stays away.

For chili on 2 mu, I will also use hybrid seed. I will apply 19 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 13 kg potassium per mu. Chili needs potassium for the fruit to set well. I will irrigate 6 times and spray 4 times. Expected yield is 2000 kg per mu.

Winter wheat on 4.1 mu: I plant improved Lunxuan seed in October. I apply 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I split the nitrogen — half at sowing, half at jointing. I irrigate 3 times: winter, jointing, and heading. I spray twice for disease. Expected yield is 500 kg per mu.

Summer maize on the same 4.1 mu: right after wheat harvest, I plant hybrid seed. There is no time to plough, so I do no-tillage sowing. I apply 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate 2 times, 3 if July is very dry. I spray twice for armyworm. Expected yield is 550 kg per mu.

I worry about costs. Fertilizer prices went up again this spring. But my uncle told me it is better to waste 50 yuan of fertilizer than to lose 500 yuan of yield. So I would rather apply a bit too much, especially on eggplant and chili, because they are my cash crops. A bad vegetable year means I cannot pay for my child's school expenses. For wheat and maize, the margin is thin, but I need them for food and feed, so I keep the inputs steady. I have well water, so I do not fight over canal schedules. I do most work myself and with my wife. For eggplant transplanting and harvest, I hire 2 or 3 workers for a few days at 150 yuan per day.
